recent_articles.title: Rajya Sabha polls: Only 4 BJP candidates in fray, party eyes clean sweep | Ahmedabad News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **BJP** candidates Raju Shukla, Mukesh Rathva, Mansinh Parmar, and Jitendra Kanzariya filed their nominations for the four Rajya Sabha seats in Gujarat on Monday.  The ruling party is expected to sweep the election uncontested as only four nominations were submitted by the deadline of June 8th. The scrutiny of the nomination papers will take place on June 9th, with the final results announced on June 11th. **Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel**, **Deputy CM Harsh Sanghavi**, state party president **Jagdish Vishwakarma**, and state organizing secretary **Ratnakar** were among those present during the nominations filing.  The election for these seats is being held due to the end of the six-year term of four Rajya Sabha MPs, including Congress leader **Shaktisinh Gohil**.

recent_articles.title: Gujarat cabinet approves ‘wire-free city mission’; ₹500 crore allocated for first phase - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Gujarat**'s Cabinet approved the ambitious 'Gujarat Wire-Free City Mission', a statewide initiative to shift overhead electricity lines underground by 2030. The project, aimed at creating smart, green and resilient cities, will involve converting over 14,600 circuit kilometers of high-tension (HT) and over 31,400 circuit kilometers of low-tension (LT) distribution lines across urban areas.  The initial phase, focusing on converting existing 11 kV overhead lines into underground cable networks, is expected to cost ₹500 crore. **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**'s vision for smart cities was cited as a driving force behind the project. The initiative aims to improve public safety and resilience against natural disasters while enhancing the reliability and quality of electricity supply.

recent_articles.title: Gujarat CM participates in toy collection drive for underprivileged children - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel** participated in a toy collection drive called "Let Kids Play, Let Kids Bloom" at Aarohi Twins Bungalow in Bopal-Ghuma. The campaign, inspired by **Union Home Minister Amit Shah**, encourages donations of unused toys from well-off families to underprivileged children.  **Patel** emphasized the importance of play and social responsibility in fostering empathy and compassion among youth. He urged citizens to contribute generously to bring joy to children from economically weaker sections.

recent_articles.title: Strictly monitor & report demographic changes in border districts: Amit Shah to DMs | India News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Amit Shah**, **Union Home and Cooperation Minister**, directed district magistrates (DMs) in border districts of Gujarat to closely monitor demographic changes.  The meeting, held in Bhuj on Friday during **Shah's** visit to the Kutch district, also emphasized the need for effective security coordination between various agencies like the BSF, Coast Guard, Income Tax, ED, and the Lead Bank Manager. **Shah** urged DMs to implement government schemes in border villages and stressed the importance of vigilance over hawala transactions, financial dealings, and suspicious activities.

recent_articles.title: 2,792 MoUs inked at Vibrant Gujarat regional conference; expected to create 2.82 lakh jobs - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Gujarat's Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi** announced that **2,792 memoranda of understanding (MoUs)** were signed during the Vibrant Gujarat Regional Conference for South Gujarat, generating an investment of ₹3,53,306 crore and promising 2.82 lakh direct jobs. The agreements are expected to be implemented over the next three years as part of the state government's efforts to expand the Vibrant Gujarat initiative beyond Gandhinagar under **Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel**.

recent_articles.title: 66% turnout for civic polls as people brave heat to vote in Gujarat - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Voter turnout in the Gujarat local body elections ranged from 45% to 66%, with **Union Home Minister Amit Shah** and **Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel** casting their votes.  Municipal corporations, including Ahmedabad, saw lower turnout compared to other local bodies. The elections are being held under revised norms for Other Backward Classes (OBC) reservations following delimitation and restructuring of wards in several districts. A total of 9,992 candidates are vying for positions across 15 municipal corporations, 84 municipalities, 34 district panchayats, and 260 taluka panchayats. The counting is scheduled for April 28th.

recent_articles.title: 66% turnout for civic polls as people brave heat to vote in Gujarat - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Voter turnout in the Gujarat local body elections ranged from 45% to 66%, with **Amit Shah** and **Bhupendra Patel** casting their votes.  The elections, held under revised norms for OBC reservations, saw a higher turnout in taluka panchayats (65.91%) and district panchayats (65.40%) compared to municipal corporations, including Ahmedabad (45.35%). The BJP, Congress, AAP, and AIMIM are the main contenders in the elections, which will be followed by counting on April 28th.  Three deaths occurred during the voting process, including an AAP candidate and a panchayat staffer.

recent_articles.title: CM Patel flags ‘nation first’ ideology; BJP hits out at Kharge at foundation day event - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Bhupendra Patel**, **Gujarat Chief Minister**, and **Jagdish Vishwakarma**, the state BJP president, addressed party workers at the 47th Foundation Day celebrations.  Patel emphasized the BJP's commitment to serving the nation with a "nation first" approach while urging calm in response to rumors and misinformation. He praised Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** and **Amit Shah** for their leadership and highlighted the state's economic growth under the BJP's rule. Vishwakarma stressed the party's dedication to democratic values and its commitment to national pride, calling for intensified efforts ahead of upcoming local body elections.

recent_articles.title: Air India Ahmedabad plane crash: Families of AI171 crash victims seek release of black box data, write to PM PM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Bereaved families** of the victims of the Air India plane crash in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, have written to **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, requesting the release of the Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR) and Flight Data Recorder (FDR) data. The families, who met on Saturday, April 4th, 2026, expressed their desire to understand the cause of the crash and sought transparency from authorities like the **Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB)**, **Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA)**, and **Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel**.  They also criticized the airline's website for its lack of clarity and accessibility.

recent_articles.title: Gujarat Government tables UCC Bill in Assembly - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Gujarat**'s government introduced the "Gujarat Uniform Civil Code, 2026" Bill in its Legislative Assembly, proposing a common legal framework for marriage, divorce, succession, and live-in relationships across religions. The bill, tabled by Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel, follows a state-appointed panel's report on UCC implementation and would make **Gujarat** the second state in India to enact such legislation after **Uttarakhand**.  The proposed law will apply to residents within the state and those residing outside its borders.

recent_articles.title: Gujarat, Centre sign MoU under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Bhupendra Patel**, Chief Minister of Gujarat, and **C. R. Patil**, Union Jal Shakti Minister, signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation for the implementation of Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0. The agreement aims to expand and manage drinking water supply systems in rural areas of the state, focusing on strengthening, regularizing, and sustaining water supply up to 2028.  The MoU outlines measures for implementation, monitoring, and transparency, including continuous water supply, completion of schemes, and village-level management. **Ishwarsinh Patel**, Minister of State for Water Supply, also participated in the virtual signing ceremony.
